title: The blindfolded man led home (6.14)
hook: a man is led away blindfolded and left in the wilderness; someone unties him and points, and he asks his way home, village by village
tomorrow: the dying man and the fire ordeal

segments.voice: Yesterday: Being, unseen yet truly here, salty, salty, salty. Your line was salty, salty, salty. Did you taste the water in the morning? Today ends week three of year two. Day three hundred fifty.

Shvetaketu has heard about honey and rivers, trees and seeds and salt. And still, maybe, he's thinking what anyone would think. Fine. Being is everywhere, and I am that. So why don't I feel it? Why am I still lost? His father doesn't scold him, and he doesn't repeat the salt one more time. He tells him about a man led far from home with a cloth tied over his eyes.
screen: `HONEY, RIVERS, TREES, SEEDS, SALT.` → `SO WHY DON'T I FEEL IT?` → `A MAN WITH A CLOTH OVER HIS EYES.`

segments.voice: Suppose, Uddalaka says, someone leads a man away from his home in Gandhara with his eyes covered, and leaves him in a lonely, empty place. The man turns and shouts, east, north, south: I was brought here blindfolded and left here blindfolded! Then someone comes along, unties the cloth, and says: Gandhara is that way. Go. And the man, asking from village to village, informed and thinking for himself, gets all the way home. In the same way, Uddalaka says, a person who has a teacher knows. Notice who does what. The stranger doesn't carry the man home. He takes off the blindfold and points. The man still has to walk, and ask, and use his own head, village after village. A teacher, in this picture, isn't a taxi. A teacher is someone who points. And notice what the man lacked. Not legs, not a road. Gandhara was there the whole time. He just couldn't see which way to turn. Uddalaka adds that, for such a person, the only delay is until he's released from the body; then he arrives. And the refrain: you are that, Shvetaketu. This week, in order. Sleep, the bird coming back to where it's tied. The honey, where no juice knows its tree. Samudra. The tree that bleeds and lives. Anima, and nothing inside. Being in the salt. And today, the blindfold untied. Seven lessons, one teaching, and a father pointing the way.
screen: `BLINDFOLDED AND LEFT ALONE.` · `SOMEONE UNTIES IT AND POINTS.` · `HE ASKS, VILLAGE BY VILLAGE.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `ONE WITH A TEACHER KNOWS.`

segments.voice: Today's practice remembers who pointed. Sit and settle. Think of someone who untied a blindfold for you: a teacher, a grandparent, a friend, an author, someone who said one sentence that turned you around. See their face. Remember what they said or did. Notice that they didn't walk the road for you. They pointed, and you walked. Let gratitude rise, if it's there. The bell holds the time.
Acharyavan, one who has a teacher. Untied and pointed toward Gandhara, he asks his way village by village; so one who has a teacher knows.
Your line: someone points the way. Today, thank one person who once pointed you in a direction, with a message, a call, or a word. Day three hundred fifty.

screen: `DAY 350 COUNTS.` → `WEEK THREE OF YEAR TWO, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: THE DYING MAN AND THE FIRE ORDEAL.`

howItsDone: Hindu traditions give the guru, the teacher, a place of honor, and many communities observe Guru Purnima each year to give thanks to their teachers.

fork.setup: you're the man from Gandhara. someone unties your blindfold and points: home is that way. what do you do?
options: wait for them to take you there.
walk, asking your way from village to village.
fork.reveal: informed and thinking for himself, he asks village by village, and reaches home. so, Uddalaka says, one with a teacher knows.

original.note: Sanskrit ācāryavān: one who has a teacher. ācāryavān puruṣo veda: a person with a teacher knows.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about a kidnapping.
what it means: the way home is there; what's missing is sight. a teacher unties the blindfold and points, and the walking is still ours.
what a scholar hears: Chandogya 6.14.1–3; Gandhara was a region in the northwest of the subcontinent; acharyavan purusho veda, a person with a teacher knows, is the lesson's key line.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 6.14.1–3 (the man from Gandhara; acharyavan purusho veda)
